```{r, include=F, warning=F, message=F, eval = F}
validation_trees %>%

  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
```

## NSVB setup

now that we have a species classification framework, We will test out a method for estimating volume based for the spatial tree list from `cloud2trees`

We're going to attempt to use the [US National Scale Volume Biomass (NSVB) models](https://doi.org/10.2737/WO-GTR-104) to predict tree volume, biomass, and carbon. We'll implement code and functionality made available by Matthew Russell at [https://github.com/mbrussell/NSVB](https://github.com/mbrussell/NSVB).

since the files and code at [https://github.com/mbrussell/NSVB](https://github.com/mbrussell/NSVB) are not released as a package (and also include the requirement to set a working directory), we'll need to create a workflow to download the files and data, update the directories in the file that defines the functions, and then load the functions using `base::source()`. also, the `nsvb.Rmd` [file](https://github.com/mbrussell/NSVB/blob/35c58efb170ecc9dd4c59502d8af7bb925b2e56d/nsvb.Rmd) from that repository isn't entirely a collection of functions but a mix of function definitions and demonstrations, so we need to define the `tree` data used during some parts of that script.

The `nsvb.Rmd` script cannot be run immediately out of the box due to configuration dependencies including:

* **Hardcoded Paths**: It explicitly contains `setwd("my/directory")`.	It will error out immediately unless rewritten to match your local folders.
* **Undefined Data Paths**:	It attempts to load several data tables (e.g., REF_SPECIES.csv, Table S1a_volib_coefs_spcd.csv).	If these files aren't in the working directory, it will throw a file not found error.
* **Dependant Workspace Objects**: It performs operations like `dplyr::inner_join(tree, spp_vol_ib_all)` without declaring what `tree` is.	It assumes a dataframe named `tree` with predefined columns already exists in the active workspace environment.

we need to do some cleanup of the `nsvb.Rmd` script so that we can at least load the data and functions it defines. then, maybe we can use the functionality with our own tree list data

```{r, include=F, eval=F}

  )
  # Do you want to create anyway? .... For sure

  # nsvb.R has hardcoded paths... fix its internal working directory path
  script_dir_temp <- file.path(nsvb_dir_temp, "NSVB", "westfall gtr", "WO-GTR-104-Supp1")
  nsvb_f_temp  <- file.path(script_dir_temp, "nsvb.R")
  # if(file.exists(nsvb_f_temp)){
    lines_temp <- readLines(nsvb_f_temp, warn = FALSE)
    # lines_temp %>% head(n=11)
    
    # relative path

    # rel_script_dir_temp
    
    # columns in some nebulous "tree" dataframe
    tree_df_temp <- 
      paste0(
        "tree <- base::data.frame("
        , "EXAMPLE = base::numeric(0), "
        , "DIVISION = base::character(0), "
        , "PROVINCE = base::character(0), "
        , "STDORGCD = base::logical(0), "
        , "SPCD = base::numeric(0), "
        , "DIA = base::numeric(0), "
        , "HT = base::numeric(0), "
        , "ACTUALHT = base::numeric(0), "
        , "CR = base::numeric(0), "
        , "CULL = base::numeric(0), "
        , "DECAYCD = base::numeric(0), "
        , "STATUSCD = base::numeric(0), "
        , "Westfall_vol = base::numeric(0), "
        , "Westfall_bio = base::numeric(0), "
        , "Westfall_c = base::numeric(0)"
        , ")"
      )
    # tree_df_temp
    
    # add it
    lines_temp <- c(tree_df_temp, lines_temp)
    # lines_temp %>% head(n=11)
    
    # overwrite the hardcoded setwd() with our new local directory path
    updt_lines_temp <-
      stringr::str_replace(
        lines_temp
        , pattern     = "setwd.*" 
        , replacement = sprintf('setwd("%s")', rel_script_dir_temp) # safely enclose path
      )
    writeLines(updt_lines_temp, nsvb_f_temp)
  }else{
    stop(paste0("oops, can't find `",nsvb_f_temp,"` "))
  }

  # source it to load the functions
  source_script_wo_dir_change_fn <- function(file_path) {
    old_dir <- getwd()
    on.exit(setwd(old_dir)) # always restore initial working directory
    source(file = file_path)
  }
  
  source_script_wo_dir_change_fn(nsvb_f_temp)
```

```{r}
source_script_wo_dir_change_fn <- function(file_path) {
  old_dir <- getwd()
  on.exit(setwd(old_dir)) # always restore initial working directory
  source(knitr::purl(file_path, quiet = T))
}

# usethis::use_data() makes it easy to save package data in the correct format
# https://r-pkgs.org/data.html#sec-data-sysdata
# doing this, make R store the data in your package’s internal data in R/sysdata.rda, so they are lazy-loaded on demand.

# but for this, we'll actually load them into the working environment by sourcing the nsvb.Rmd file
# nsvb_f_temp
source_script_wo_dir_change_fn(nsvb_f_temp)
# clean up from knitr::purl()
if(file.exists(file.path(getwd(),"nsvb.R"))){
  unlink(file.path(getwd(),"nsvb.R"))
}
```

## NSVB Gross Values

while the `nsvb.Rmd` file contains function definitions, it is more of a procedural template script. let's try to figure out what we need to work with our own tree data

to get the primary **Gross** volume metrics of:

| Westfall abbr      | FIADB abbr | Definition      | Units |
| ----------- | ----------- | ----------- | ----------- |
| $h_{m}$	| - |	Merchantable height to a 4.0 inch top      | feet       |
| $R_{1}$	| - |		Proportion of volume to 1 foot (i.e., stump)      | -       |
| $R_{m}$	| -	 |	Proportion of volume to the merchantable height (i.e., 4.0 inches)      | -       |
| $R_{s}$ |	-	| Proportion of volume to sawlog top (7.0 inches for softwoods; 9.0 inches for hardwoods)      | -       |
| $Vtot_{ib}Gross$      | VOLTSGRS       | Gross cubic-foot total-stem wood volume      | cubic feet       |
| $Vtot_{bk}Gross$	| VOLTSGRS_BARK	| Gross cubic-foot total-stem bark volume      | cubic feet       |
| $Vmer_{ib}Gross$ | 	VOLCFGRS	 |	Gross cubic-foot merchantable stem wood volume (inside bark)      | cubic feet       |
| $Vmer_{bk}Gross$ |	VOLCFGRS_BARK	 |	Merchantable stem bark volume      | cubic feet       |
| $Vsaw_{ib}Gross$ |	VOLCSGRS	 |	Gross cubic-foot wood volume in the sawlog portion of a sawtimber tree      | cubic feet       |
| $Vsaw_{bk}Gross$ |	VOLCSGRS_BARK	Gross |	 cubic-foot bark volume in the sawlog portion of a sawtimber tree      | cubic feet       |
| $Vstump_{ib}Gross$ |	VOLCFGRS_STUMP |		Gross cubic-foot stump wood volume (inside bark)      | cubic feet       |
| $Vstump_{bk}Gross$ |	VOLCFGRS_STUMP_BARK	 |	Gross cubic-foot stump bark volume      | cubic feet       |
| $Vtop_{ib}Gross$ |	VOLCFGRS_TOP |		Gross cubic-foot stem-top wood volume, inside bark      | cubic feet       |
| $Vtop_{bk}Gross$ |	VOLCFGRS_TOP_BARK |		Gross cubic-foot stem-top bark volume, outside bark      | cubic feet       |

, we should only need basic tree information......After digging through the `nsvb.Rmd` code and Westfall et al. ([2024](https://doi.org/10.2737/WO-GTR-104)) (process outlined below), we have determined that this basic information includes: location ("DIVISION"), species ("SPCD"), planting condition ("STDORGCD"), and, of course tree height in feet ("HT") and diameter in inches ("DIA"). Merchantable volume also requires actual height ("ACTUALHT") which is the measure of the standing height compared to the derived height ("HT") which is the standing height plus the missing top height for trees with broken tops. For all point cloud-based tree list data (i.e. from `cloud2trees`) we will have actual height and never derived height adjustment for trees with broken tops.

the first thing we need to figure out is this `SPCD` data attribute which is described by Westfall et al. ([2024](https://doi.org/10.2737/WO-GTR-104)) as:

>For tree biomass prediction, the accuracy and precision of models were essentially unknown due to the pseudo-data approach used in the original research. Thus, efforts were undertaken to develop a national methodology for compatible predictions of tree volume, biomass, and carbon content (Radtke et al. 2015, 2017; Weiskittel et al. 2015) for species commonly occurring on U.S. forest land. Specifically, the targeted species are inclusive of those identified by FIA species code (SPCD) ≤999, except for those designated as woodland species (USDA Forest Service 2022). The resulting methodology is hereafter referred to as the national-scale volume and biomass (NSVB) framework. (p. 1)

we know this data! this is what we have been working so hard to get up to this point in the analysis. we'll start by using the FIA species code lookup table to get FIA species code, genus, and species for all of our data sets based on the `species_symbol` (e.g. "PIPO", "POTR5", "QURU")

```{r}
# fia_species_lookup %>% dplyr::glimpse()
# ref_trees_list
ref_trees_list <- 
  ref_trees_list %>% 
  purrr::compact() %>% 
  purrr::map(
    \(df)
    df %>% 
      # get rid of columns we'll create
      dplyr::select( -dplyr::any_of(c(
        "hey_xxxxxxxxxx"
        , "spcd"
        , "genus"
        , "species"
        , "common_name"
      ))) %>% 
      dplyr::left_join(
        fia_species_lookup %>% 
          dplyr::select(
            species_symbol
            , spcd
            , genus
            , species
            , common_name
          )
        , by = "species_symbol"
        , relationship = "many-to-one"
      )
  )
# pred_trees_list
pred_trees_list <- 
  pred_trees_list %>% 
  purrr::compact() %>% 
  purrr::map(
    \(df)
    df %>% 
      # get rid of columns we'll create
      dplyr::select( -dplyr::any_of(c(
        "hey_xxxxxxxxxx"
        , "spcd"
        , "genus"
        , "species"
        , "common_name"
      ))) %>% 
      dplyr::left_join(
        fia_species_lookup %>% 
          dplyr::select(
            species_symbol
            , spcd
            , genus
            , species
            , common_name
          )
        , by = "species_symbol"
        , relationship = "many-to-one"
      )
  )
```

the next thing is this `DIVISION` data attribute. Based on Westfall et al. ([2024](https://doi.org/10.2737/WO-GTR-104)), it looks like this refers to Ecodivisions used by Forest Inventory and Analysis for (a) 48 of the 50 United States (Source: Cleland et al. 2007) and (b) Alaska (Source: Nowacki et al. 2003). however, the current authoritative "[EcoMapDivisions](https://data-usfs.hub.arcgis.com/datasets/usfs::ecosys-ecomapdivisions-2025/about)" data set on the [USFS Geospatial Data Discovery](https://data-usfs.hub.arcgis.com/) does not align with data used in Westfall et al. ([2024](https://doi.org/10.2737/WO-GTR-104)). We need to find the older version......

........after some digging, this Ecodivision spatial data used for NSVB may still be available on the [FSGeodata Clearinghouse](https://data.fs.usda.gov/geodata/edw/datasets.php) under the title "[Ecological Sections](https://data.fs.usda.gov/geodata/edw/edw_resources/meta/Ecosys_EcomapSections_2007.xml)" and it may also available on the data discovery tool [here](https://data-usfs.hub.arcgis.com/datasets/usfs::ecological-sections-feature-layer/about)


let's load that data, clean it, and check it

```{r}
fia_ecodivisions_sf <- 
  sf::st_read("../data/Ecosys_EcomapSections_2007/S_USA.Ecosys_EcomapSections_2007.shp", quiet = T) %>%
  dplyr::rename_with(
    ~ tolower(.x) %>% 
      stringr::str_squish() %>% 
      make.names() %>% 
      stringr::str_replace_all( "\\.{2,}", ".") %>% 
      stringr::str_remove( "\\.$") %>% 
      stringr::str_replace_all( "\\.", "_")
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-map_unit_d) %>% 
  # clean this thing up to get division
  dplyr::filter(tolower(map_unit_s)!="water") %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    fia_ecodivision = 
      map_unit_s %>% 
      stringr::str_squish() %>% 
      # get just the number block and any letters at the beginning
      stringr::str_extract("^[^0-9]*\\d+") %>%
      # replace the last digit with a 0
      stringr::str_replace("\\d$", "0")
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(fia_ecodivision)) %>% 
  # union the geometries
  sf::st_make_valid() %>% 
  dplyr::filter(sf::st_is_valid(.)) %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(fia_ecodivision) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(.groups = "drop") %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    fia_ecodivision_desc = dplyr::case_when(
      fia_ecodivision == "210"  ~ "Warm Continental Division"
      , fia_ecodivision == "220"  ~ "Hot Continental Division"
      , fia_ecodivision == "230"  ~ "Subtropical Division"
      , fia_ecodivision == "240"  ~ "Marine Division"
      , fia_ecodivision == "250"  ~ "Prairie Division"
      , fia_ecodivision == "260"  ~ "Mediterranean Division"
      , fia_ecodivision == "310"  ~ "Tropical/Subtropical Steppe Division"
      , fia_ecodivision == "320"  ~ "Tropical/Subtropical Desert Division"
      , fia_ecodivision == "330"  ~ "Temperate Steppe Division"
      , fia_ecodivision == "340"  ~ "Temperate Desert Division"
      , fia_ecodivision == "410"  ~ "Savanna Division"
      , fia_ecodivision == "M210" ~ "Warm Continental Mountains"
      , fia_ecodivision == "M220" ~ "Hot Continental Mountains"
      , fia_ecodivision == "M230" ~ "Subtropical Mountains"
      , fia_ecodivision == "M240" ~ "Marine Mountains"
      , fia_ecodivision == "M260" ~ "Mediterranean Mountains"
      , fia_ecodivision == "M310" ~ "Tropical/Subtropical Steppe Mountains"
      , fia_ecodivision == "M330" ~ "Temperate Steppe Mountains"
      , fia_ecodivision == "M340" ~ "Temperate Desert Mountains"
      , TRUE ~ as.character(NA)
    )
  )
```

pretty good match with Westfall et al. ([2024](https://doi.org/10.2737/WO-GTR-104)) Fig. 1 (p. 3). we can spatially match the trees with this ecodivision spatial data now that we dug up the data from the research data archive and cleaned it up.

```{r}
# make a function to attach `fia_ecodivision` to spatial data

# first, function to check and make it spatial points
## same as cloud2trees:::check_spatial_points() but removes treeID requirement
check_spatial_points <- function(
  tree_list
  , crs = NA
){
  ##################################
  # convert to spatial points data
  ##################################
  if(inherits(tree_list, "sf")){
    # if points, just use it
    if( sf::st_is(tree_list, type = c("POINT", "MULTIPOINT")) %>% all() ){
      tree_tops <- tree_list %>% dplyr::ungroup()
    }else{ # if spatial but not points, drop geom and set to points
      tree_tops <- tree_list %>%
        dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
        sf::st_centroid()
    }
  }else{ # not spatial data
    # convert from data.frame to spatial points
    if(!inherits(tree_list, "data.frame")){
      stop("must pass a data.frame or sf object to the `tree_list` parameter")
    }
    if(is.na(crs) || is.na(readr::parse_number(as.character(crs)))){
      stop("must provide the EPSG code in `crs` parameter for the projection of x,y data")
    }
    if(
      !(stringr::str_equal(nms, "tree_x") %>% any())
      || !(stringr::str_equal(nms, "tree_y") %>% any())
    ){ # doesn't contain x,y
      stop("must provide the columns `tree_x` and `tree_y`")
    }
    tree_tops <- tree_list %>%
      dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
      sf::st_as_sf(
        coords = c("tree_x", "tree_y")
        , crs = paste0( "EPSG:", readr::parse_number(as.character(crs)) )
        , remove = F
      )
  }

  return(tree_tops)
}

### take a spatial data, or df with tree_x and tree_y, and combine with fia ecodivision
get_fia_ecodivision <- function(tree_list, fia_ecodivisions_sf, crs = NA) {
  
  # fia_ecodivisions_sf has to be spatial
  if(
    !inherits(fia_ecodivisions_sf, "sf") &&
    !all( sf::st_is(fia_ecodivisions_sf, type = c("POLYGON", "MULTIPOLYGON")) )
  ){
    stop("`fia_ecodivisions_sf` must be spatial polygons `sf` class")
  }
  if(!any(stringr::str_equal(names(fia_ecodivisions_sf),"fia_ecodivision"))){
    stop("`fia_ecodivisions_sf` must include `fia_ecodivision` column")
  }
  
  # add a join id
  if(!inherits(tree_list, "data.frame")){
    stop("must pass a data.frame or sf object to the `tree_list` parameter")
  }
  tree_list <- tree_list %>% dplyr::ungroup() %>% dplyr::mutate(xxx_join_id = dplyr::row_number())
  
  # check/make spatial points
  tree_tops <- check_spatial_points(tree_list=tree_list, crs=crs) %>% dplyr::select(xxx_join_id)
  
  # do the spatial join
  tree_tops <- 
    tree_tops %>% 
    sf::st_join(
      fia_ecodivisions_sf %>% sf::st_transform(sf::st_crs(tree_tops))
      , left = T
      , largest = T
    ) %>% 
    sf::st_drop_geometry()
  
  # add to original data without the spatial
  if(nrow(tree_tops)==0){return(tree_list %>% dplyr::select(-xxx_join_id))}
  tree_list %>% 
    # get rid of columns we'll create
    dplyr::select( -dplyr::any_of(c(
      "hey_xxxxxxxxxx"
      , "fia_ecodivision"
      , "fia_ecodivision_desc"
    ))) %>% 
    # join
    dplyr::left_join(tree_tops, by = "xxx_join_id", relationship = "one-to-one") %>% 
    dplyr::select(-xxx_join_id)
  
}
```

let's make a function to use the data loaded into our current working session when we ran `nsvb.Rmd` to get those basic volume metrics with our tree list data (both reference and predicted)

if we are going to set up an R package for NSVB, or any other method, that is highly dependent on external data (i.e. csv's), we should use `usethis::use_data(..., internal = T)`. This `usethis::use_data()` function makes it easy to save package data in [the correct format](https://r-pkgs.org/data.html#sec-data-sysdata) by making R store the data in your package’s internal data in `R/sysdata.rda` so they are lazy-loaded on demand.

this first function will focus on the NSVB **Gross** volume metrics which only require the following from the tree list: `HT`, `ACTUALHT`, `DIA`, `SPCD`, `DIVISION`, `STDORGCD`

```{r}
# tree_list <- ref_trees_list[[1]] %>% dplyr::mutate(V_mer_ib_Gross="hey")
# tree_list %>% dplyr::glimpse()
### function to set DIA in inches depending on what's in the data
cols_set_nsvb_dbh <- function(df) {
  # diameter check
  if(any(stringr::str_equal(names(df), "DIA"))){
    df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(DIA = as.numeric(DIA))
  }else if(any(stringr::str_equal(names(df), "dia"))){
    df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(DIA = as.numeric(dia))
  }else if(any(stringr::str_equal(names(df), "dbh_in"))){
    df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(DIA = as.numeric(dbh_in))
  }else if(any(stringr::str_equal(names(df), "dbh_cm"))){
    df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(DIA = as.numeric(dbh_cm)/2.54)
  }else{
    stop(paste0(
      "the data does not contain the columns `DIA`, `dbh_cm`, or `dbh_in`"
      , "\n .... at least one of these columns must be present and have data"
    ))
  }
  
  cloud2trees:::check_df_cols_all_missing(df = df, col_names = "DIA", all_numeric = T)
  
  return(df)
}
### function to set HT in feet depending on what's in the data
cols_set_nsvb_height <- function(df) {
  # height check
  if(any(stringr::str_equal(names(df), "HT"))){
    df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(HT = as.numeric(HT))
  }else if(any(stringr::str_equal(names(df), "ht"))){
    df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(HT = as.numeric(ht))
  }else if(any(stringr::str_equal(names(df), "tree_height_ft"))){
    df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(HT = as.numeric(tree_height_ft))
  }else if(any(stringr::str_equal(names(df), "tree_height_m"))){
    df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(HT = as.numeric(tree_height_m)*3.281)
  }else{
    stop(paste0(
      "the data does not contain the columns `HT`, `tree_height_m`, or `tree_height_ft`"
      , "\n .... at least one of these columns must be present and have data"
    ))
  }
  cloud2trees:::check_df_cols_all_missing(df = df, col_names = "HT", all_numeric = T)
  
  # actual height check
  if(any(stringr::str_equal(names(df), "ACTUALHT"))){
    df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(ACTUALHT = as.numeric(ACTUALHT))
  }else if(any(stringr::str_equal(names(df), "actualht"))){
    df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(ACTUALHT = actualht)
  }else if(any(stringr::str_equal(names(df), "HT"))){
    df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(ACTUALHT = HT)
    message("...setting ACTUALHT to HT")
  }else{
    stop(paste0(
      "the data does not contain the columns `ACTUALHT`"
      , "\n .... at least one of these columns must be present and have data"
    ))
  }
  cloud2trees:::check_df_cols_all_missing(df = df, col_names = "ACTUALHT", all_numeric = T)
  
  return(df)
}
### function to set SPCD depending on what's in the data
cols_set_nsvb_spcd <- function(df) {
  # SPCD check
  if(any(stringr::str_equal(names(df), "SPCD"))){
    df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(SPCD = as.numeric(SPCD))
  }else if(any(stringr::str_equal(names(df), "spcd"))){
    df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(SPCD = as.numeric(spcd))
  }else{
    stop(paste0(
      "the data does not contain the columns `SPCD` or `spcd`"
      , "\n .... at least one of these columns must be present and have data"
    ))
  }
  cloud2trees:::check_df_cols_all_missing(df = df, col_names = "SPCD", all_numeric = T)
  
  ### !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! could check against possible values from lookup table
  
  return(df)
}
### function to set DIVISION depending on what's in the data
cols_set_nsvb_division <- function(df, my_fia_ecodivisions_sf=NULL) {
  # DIVISION check
  if(any(stringr::str_equal(names(df), "DIVISION"))){
    df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate( DIVISION = stringr::str_remove_all(as.character(DIVISION),"\\s+") )
  }else if(any(stringr::str_equal(names(df), "division"))){
    df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate( DIVISION = stringr::str_remove_all(as.character(division),"\\s+") )
  }else if(any(stringr::str_equal(names(df), "fia_ecodivision"))){
    df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate( DIVISION = stringr::str_remove_all(as.character(fia_ecodivision),"\\s+") )
  }else if(
    inherits(df,"sf") &&
    inherits(my_fia_ecodivisions_sf,"sf")
    # all(c("tree_x","tree_y") %in% names(df))
  ) {
    df <- df %>% get_fia_ecodivision(fia_ecodivisions_sf = my_fia_ecodivisions_sf)
  }else{
    stop(paste0(
      "the data does not contain the columns `DIVISION` or `fia_ecodivision`"
      , "\n .... at least one of these columns must be present and have data"
    ))
  }
  cloud2trees:::check_df_cols_all_missing(df = df, col_names = "DIVISION", all_numeric = F)
  
  ### !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! could check against possible values from lookup table
  
  return(df)
}
### function to set STDORGCD depending on what's in the data
cols_set_nsvb_stdorgcd <- function(df, default_val = NA){
  default_val <- dplyr::coalesce(as.integer(default_val), as.integer(NA))
  # STDORGCD check
  if(any(stringr::str_equal(names(df), "STDORGCD"))){
    df <- df
  }else if(any(stringr::str_equal(names(df), "stdorgcd"))){
    df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(STDORGCD = stdorgcd)
  }else if(T){ ### !!!! this just sets it to a default
    df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(STDORGCD = default_val)
  }else{
    stop(paste0(
      "the data does not contain the columns `STDORGCD`"
      , "\n .... at least one of these columns must be present and have data"
    ))
  }
  
  # check valid values
  if(any( dplyr::coalesce(df$STDORGCD,0)%%1 != 0 )){stop("STDORGCD must be integer without decimal values")}
  if(!all( df$STDORGCD %in% c(1,0,NA) )){stop("STDORGCD must be integer value of 1, 0, or NA")}
  
  # do it as int
  df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(STDORGCD = dplyr::coalesce(as.integer(STDORGCD), default_val))

  return(df)
}

# function to get all nsvb gross stuff
trees_nsvb_volume_gross <- function(
  tree_list
  , default_stdorgcd = NA
){
  # add check for fia_ecodivisions_sf like checks for treemap data
  fia_ecodivisions_sf <- NULL

  # save name for later
  orig_names_temp <- names(tree_list)
  
  # set up HT, ACTUALHT, and DIA
  # will also check and throw error if missing
  tree_list <- tree_list %>% 
    cols_set_nsvb_dbh() %>% 
    cols_set_nsvb_height() %>% 
    cols_set_nsvb_spcd() %>% 
    cols_set_nsvb_division(my_fia_ecodivisions_sf = fia_ecodivisions_sf) %>% 
    cols_set_nsvb_stdorgcd(default_val = default_stdorgcd)
  
  if(
    !all(c("HT", "ACTUALHT", "DIA", "SPCD", "DIVISION", "STDORGCD") %in% names(tree_list))
  ){
    stop("missing NSVB calculation columns in `tree_list`")
  }
  # we need a clean data set that doesn't include any variables named in any of the data used by the nsvb.Rmd data sets or functions
  # we'll start with the absolute minimum data, go through the nsvb process, drop any cols in our original data created in the process
  # then join on the new data
  # add a join id for use in combining in case any nsvb process drops rows
  tree_list <- tree_list %>% 
    dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(xxx_join_id = dplyr::row_number())
  
  tree_list_w_nsvb <- 
    tree_list %>%
    sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
    dplyr::select(xxx_join_id, HT, ACTUALHT, DIA, SPCD, DIVISION, STDORGCD)
  # save the names so we know what was added
  hey_names_temp <- names(tree_list_w_nsvb)

  ######################################################################################################
  # GW add: there are records by DIVISION and SPCD that do not have full representation across all
  # possible values of STDORGCD : for planted (stand origin code (STDORGCD) = 1) and natural (STDORGCD = 0)
  # we need STDORGCD = NA,0,1 rows for all possible DIVISION + SPCD combinations
  # to do this, we'll just pick one record from the `spp_vol_ib_all` table (and other tables) prioritizing:
  # 1) NA (not origin specific); 2) natural (STDORGCD = 0); 3) planted (STDORGCD = 1)
  # ....
  # the tables have all possible combinations of DIVISION, SPCD (see spp_vol_division_na definition)
  # ... so, we just need to join by DIVISION, SPCD and pick just one set of coeffs for incomplete STDORGCD
  ######################################################################################################
  spp_vol_ib_all_div_spcd_gw <- 
    spp_vol_ib_all %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(
      STDORGCD = ifelse(is.na(STDORGCD), -1, STDORGCD)
    ) %>% 
    dplyr::group_by(DIVISION,SPCD) %>% 
    dplyr::slice_min(n=1, order_by = STDORGCD, with_ties = F) %>% 
    dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
    dplyr::select(-STDORGCD)
    
  spp_vol_bark_all_div_spcd_gw <- 
    spp_vol_bark_all %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(
      STDORGCD = ifelse(is.na(STDORGCD), -1, STDORGCD)
    ) %>% 
    dplyr::group_by(DIVISION,SPCD) %>% 
    dplyr::slice_min(n=1, order_by = STDORGCD, with_ties = F) %>% 
    dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
    dplyr::select(-STDORGCD)
  
  spp_vol_ob_all_div_spcd_gw <- 
    spp_vol_ob_all %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(
      STDORGCD = ifelse(is.na(STDORGCD), -1, STDORGCD)
    ) %>% 
    dplyr::group_by(DIVISION,SPCD) %>% 
    dplyr::slice_min(n=1, order_by = STDORGCD, with_ties = F) %>% 
    dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
    dplyr::select(-STDORGCD)
    
  spp_vol_ratio_all_div_spcd_gw <- 
    spp_vol_ratio_all %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(
      STDORGCD = ifelse(is.na(STDORGCD), -1, STDORGCD)
    ) %>% 
    dplyr::group_by(DIVISION,SPCD) %>% 
    dplyr::slice_min(n=1, order_by = STDORGCD, with_ties = F) %>% 
    dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
    dplyr::select(-STDORGCD)
  
  ######################################################################################################
  # GW add: there are records for SPCD that do not have any data because they are not "timber"
  # e.g. QUGA (Quercus gambelii), spcd: 814
  # for those records, the nsvb.Rmd functions (e.g., get_nsvb()) will throw an error
  # we don't want this
  # our options are to 
  #   1) use the nsvb.Rmd tables to work with only species that are represented in the data (e.g. spp_vol_ib_all)
        # then join back on to full tree_list data with NA for all nsvb cols
  #   2) work with the full data and simply catch the error and NA the value if a function errors
  # ...
  # ... let's do 2
  ######################################################################################################
  safe_get_nsvb <- purrr::possibly(get_nsvb, otherwise = NA)
  safe_get_hm <- purrr::possibly(get_hm, otherwise = NA)
  safe_get_V_ratio <- purrr::possibly(get_V_ratio, otherwise = NA)
  ######################################################################################################
  # this method is defined in nsvb.Rmd
  # from https://github.com/mbrussell/NSVB
  # copied with slight adjustments
  ######################################################################################################
  nsvb_join_cols_temp <- c("DIVISION", "STDORGCD", "SPCD")
  tree_list_w_nsvb <- 
    tree_list_w_nsvb %>% 
    dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
    # 1. Gross total stem wood volume, inside bark:
    dplyr::left_join(spp_vol_ib_all, by = nsvb_join_cols_temp) %>% 
    ### !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! GW add ###
    dplyr::rows_patch(spp_vol_ib_all_div_spcd_gw, by = c("DIVISION","SPCD"), unmatched = "ignore") %>% 
    ### !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! GW add end ###
    dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(
      V_tot_ib_Gross = safe_get_nsvb(
        MODEL = MODEL
        , SPCD = SPCD
        , DIA = DIA
        , HT = HT
        , a = a, a1 = a1, b = b
        , b1 = b1, c = c, c1 = c1
        , WDSG = NA
      )
      , 
    ) %>% 
    dplyr::select(
      -base::setdiff(names(spp_vol_ib_all),nsvb_join_cols_temp) 
    ) %>% 
    dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
    # 2. Gross total stem bark volume
    dplyr::left_join(spp_vol_bark_all, by = nsvb_join_cols_temp) %>% 
    ### !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! GW add ###
    dplyr::rows_patch(spp_vol_bark_all_div_spcd_gw, by = c("DIVISION","SPCD"), unmatched = "ignore") %>% 
    ### !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! GW add end ###
    dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(
      V_tot_bk_Gross = safe_get_nsvb(
        MODEL = MODEL
        , SPCD = SPCD
        , DIA = DIA
        , HT = HT
        , a = a, a1 = a1, b = b
        , b1 = b1, c = c, c1 = c1
        , WDSG = NA
      )
      # 3. Gross total stem outside-bark volume
      , V_tot_ob_Gross = V_tot_ib_Gross + V_tot_bk_Gross
    ) %>% 
    dplyr::select(
      -base::setdiff(names(spp_vol_bark_all),nsvb_join_cols_temp) 
    ) %>% 
    dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
    # 4. Estimate height to merchantable top diameter (4.0-inch)
    dplyr::left_join(spp_vol_ob_all, by = nsvb_join_cols_temp) %>% 
    ### !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! GW add ###
    dplyr::rows_patch(spp_vol_ob_all_div_spcd_gw, by = c("DIVISION","SPCD"), unmatched = "ignore") %>% 
    ### !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! GW add end ###
    dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(
      hm = ifelse(
        DIA >= 5
        , safe_get_hm(
          top_dia = 4
          , a = a, b = b, c = c
          , alpha = alpha, beta = beta
          , DIA = DIA, HT = HT
        )
        , NA
      )
    ) %>% 
    dplyr::select(
      -base::setdiff(names(spp_vol_ob_all),nsvb_join_cols_temp) 
    ) %>% 
    dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
    # 5. Estimate merchantable wood volume – volume ratios to stump & merchantable top
    dplyr::left_join(spp_vol_ratio_all, by = nsvb_join_cols_temp) %>% 
    ### !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! GW add ###
    dplyr::rows_patch(spp_vol_ratio_all_div_spcd_gw, by = c("DIVISION","SPCD"), unmatched = "ignore") %>% 
    ### !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! GW add end ###
    dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(
      R_1 = safe_get_V_ratio(h1 = 1, HT = HT, alpha = alpha, beta = beta)
      , R_m = ifelse(
        DIA >= 5
        , safe_get_V_ratio(
          h1 = hm, HT = HT
          , alpha = alpha, beta = beta
        )
        , NA
      )
      , R_m_2 = safe_get_V_ratio(
        h1 = ACTUALHT, HT = HT
        , alpha = alpha, beta = beta
      )
      , V_mer_ib_Gross = (R_m * V_tot_ib_Gross ) - (R_1 * V_tot_ib_Gross)
      , V_mer_ob_Gross = (R_m * V_tot_ob_Gross ) - (R_1 * V_tot_ob_Gross)
      , V_mer_bk_Gross = V_mer_ob_Gross - V_mer_ib_Gross
    ) %>% 
    dplyr::select(
      -base::setdiff(names(spp_vol_ratio_all),nsvb_join_cols_temp) 
    ) %>% 
    dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
    # Volume in the sawlog portion of the stem
    dplyr::left_join(spp_vol_ob_all, by = nsvb_join_cols_temp) %>% 
    ### !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! GW add ###
    dplyr::rows_patch(spp_vol_ob_all_div_spcd_gw, by = c("DIVISION","SPCD"), unmatched = "ignore") %>% 
    ### !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! GW add end ###
    dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(
      hm_saw = ifelse(
        SPCD < 300 & DIA >= 9.0
        , safe_get_hm(
          top_dia = 7
          , a = a, b = b, c = c
          , alpha = alpha, beta = beta
          , DIA = DIA, HT = HT
        )
        , ifelse(
          SPCD >= 300 & DIA >= 11.0
          , safe_get_hm(
            top_dia = 9
            , a = a, b = b, c = c
            , alpha = alpha, beta = beta
            , DIA = DIA, HT = HT
          )
          , NA
        )
      )
    ) %>% 
    dplyr::select(
      -base::setdiff(names(spp_vol_ob_all),nsvb_join_cols_temp) 
    ) %>% 
    dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
    # Sawlog volumes ratios - stump and merchantable height
    dplyr::left_join(spp_vol_ratio_all, by = nsvb_join_cols_temp) %>% 
    ### !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! GW add ###
    dplyr::rows_patch(spp_vol_ratio_all_div_spcd_gw, by = c("DIVISION","SPCD"), unmatched = "ignore") %>% 
    ### !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! GW add end ###
    dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(
      R_s = safe_get_V_ratio(
        h1 = hm_saw
        , HT = HT
        , alpha = alpha
        , beta = beta
      )
    ) %>% 
    dplyr::select(
      -base::setdiff(names(spp_vol_ratio_all),nsvb_join_cols_temp) 
    ) %>% 
    dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
    # More tree-level calcs here
    #### GW add.... i'm going to break this into columns that require CULL and those that don't
    dplyr::mutate(
      V_saw_ib_Gross = (R_s * V_tot_ib_Gross) - (R_1 * V_tot_ib_Gross)
      , V_saw_ob_Gross = (R_s * V_tot_ob_Gross) - (R_1 * V_tot_ob_Gross)
      , V_saw_bk_Gross = V_saw_ob_Gross - V_saw_ib_Gross
      , V_stump_ob_Gross = (R_1 * V_tot_ob_Gross)
      , V_stump_ib_Gross = (R_1 * V_tot_ib_Gross)
      , V_stump_bk_Gross = V_stump_ob_Gross - V_stump_ib_Gross
      , V_top_ob_Gross = V_tot_ob_Gross - V_mer_ob_Gross - V_stump_ob_Gross
      , V_top_ib_Gross = V_tot_ib_Gross - V_mer_ib_Gross - V_stump_ib_Gross
      , V_top_bk_Gross = V_top_ob_Gross - V_top_ib_Gross
    )
    # #### GW add.... these aren't defined in Westfall or https://github.com/mbrussell/NSVB
    # dplyr::select(
    #   -c(
    #     R_m_2, hm_saw
    #   )
    # )

  ######################################################################################################
  # add nsvb volume to original data
  ######################################################################################################
  new_names_temp <- base::setdiff(names(tree_list_w_nsvb),hey_names_temp)
  
  tree_list <-
    tree_list %>% 
    # get rid of columns we'll create
    dplyr::select( -dplyr::any_of(c(
      "hey_xxxxxxxxxx"
      , new_names_temp
    ))) %>% 
    # add nsvb data
    dplyr::left_join(
      tree_list_w_nsvb %>% dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(
        "xxx_join_id"
        , new_names_temp
      )))
      , by = "xxx_join_id"
      , relationship = "one-to-one"
    ) %>% 
    # clean up cols we may have created
    dplyr::select(-xxx_join_id) %>% 
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(
      base::setdiff(orig_names_temp,new_names_temp)
      , new_names_temp
    )))
  
  # return
  return(tree_list)
}
```

## NSVB Modified "Sound" Values

let's try to figure out what we need to work with our own tree data

to get the **Modified** "Sound" volume metrics of:

| Westfall abbr      | FIADB abbr | Definition      | Units |
| ----------- | ----------- | ----------- | ----------- |
| $Vtot_{ib}Sound$ |	VOLTSSND |		Sound cubic-foot total-stem wood volume, inside bark      | cubic feet       |
| $Vtot_{bk}Sound$ |	VOLTSSND_BARK	 |	Sound cubic-foot total-stem bark volume      | cubic feet       |
| $Vstump_{ib}Sound$ |	VOLCFSND_STUMP |		Sound cubic-foot stump wood volume      | cubic feet       |
| $Vstump_{bk}Sound$ |	VOLCFSND_STUMP_BARK |		Sound cubic-foot stump bark volume      | cubic feet       |
| $Vmer_{ib}Sound$ |	VOLCFSND |		Sound cubic-foot stem wood volume      | cubic feet       |
| $Vmer_{bk}Sound$ |	VOLCFSND_BARK |		Sound cubic-foot stem bark volume      | cubic feet       |
| $Vtop_{ib}Sound$ |	VOLCFSND_TOP |		Sound cubic-foot stem-top wood volume      | cubic feet       |
| $Vtop_{bk}$ |	VOLCFSND_TOP_BARK |		Sound cubic-foot stem-top bark volume      | cubic feet       |
| $Vsaw_{ib}Sound$ |	VOLCSSND |		Sound cubic-foot wood volume in the sawlog portion of a sawtimber tree      | cubic feet       |
| $Vsaw_{bk}Sound$ |	VOLCSSND_BARK |		Sound cubic-foot bark volume in the sawlog portion of a sawtimber tree      | cubic feet       |

Westfall et al. ([2024](https://doi.org/10.2737/WO-GTR-104)) outline modifications and reductions applied to volume (and subsequent biomass) estimates based on wood decay classification for standing dead trees and broken top trees:

the first relevant for our present analysis section:

>Notationally, values designated as "Sound" hereafter refer to values occurring after considering any deductions due to cull, broken top, or dead tree density reductions (p. 10)

some more detail:

>Modifications for standing dead trees to wood density and for bark and branch losses based on the observed level of decay as indicated by the FIA decay class code (DECAYCD) variable (Burrill et al. 2023) and hardwood or softwood species classification are incorporated into the NSVB framework by adopting the findings of Harmon et al. (2011) as shown in table 1. Note that these values account for differences between hardwood and softwood species, unlike the values presented in Domke et al. (2011). The values for wood density proportion for DECAYCD = 3 are also used to account for the fact that rotten wood cull still maintains a weight greater than zero even though rotten cull is entirely deducted to obtain sound cubic volume amounts. In this case, the observed cull is assumed to be entirely rotten wood, and the density of that wood is reduced accordingly. In addition, model 6 is used to implement a standardized approach to estimate volume and biomass reductions from missing stem tops. Belowground coarse root biomass is calculated using the approach described in Heath et al. (2009) but by using merchantable stem wood volume as calculated here and applying the wood density proportions from table 1 for standing dead trees. (p. 4-5)

these modified **Sound** volume estimates rely on the **Gross** predictions detailed above as well as the tree list inputs required to calculate those predictions (`HT`, `ACTUALHT`, `DIA`, `SPCD`, `DIVISION`, `STDORGCD`). however, they also rely on other variables with information about the tree status which include: 

* `CULL` : is the percentage, on a scale from 0 to 100 (percentage points), of rotten/missing wood in the main stem below any missing top (p. 10).
* `STATUSCD` : Status code indicating whether the tree is live (`STATUSCD = 1`), dead (`STATUSCD = 2`), or cut (`STATUSCD = 3`) at the time of measurement

let's define a function to get these modified **Sound** values

```{r}
# tree_list <- pred_trees_list[[1]]
# tree_list %>% dplyr::glimpse()

### function to set CULL depending on what's in the data
cols_set_nsvb_cull <- function(df, default_val = 0){
  default_val <- dplyr::coalesce(as.numeric(default_val), 0)
  # CULL check
  if(any(stringr::str_equal(names(df), "CULL"))){
    df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(CULL = as.numeric(CULL))
  }else if(any(stringr::str_equal(names(df), "cull"))){
    df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(CULL = as.numeric(cull))
  }else if(T){ ### !!!! this just sets it to a default
    df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(CULL = default_val)
  }else{
    stop(paste0(
      "the data does not contain the columns `CULL`"
      , "\n .... at least one of these columns must be present and have data"
    ))
  }
  
  ## CULL should be on 0-100 scale...check and fix if a user put it in on 0-1 scale (as decimals..)
  df <- 
    df %>% 
    dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(
      xxxx_not_na_zero = !is.na(CULL) & CULL != 0 # all values defined
      , xxxx_has_dec = xxxx_not_na_zero & (CULL%%1 != 0) & (CULL<1) # defined values less than 1 that are decimals
      # prop of vals with decimals
      , xxxx_prop_dec = sum(xxxx_has_dec, na.rm = T) / sum(xxxx_not_na_zero, na.rm = T)
      , xxxx_prop_dec = dplyr::coalesce(xxxx_prop_dec,0)
      # if over half of defined values are less than one and have decimals, convert to 0-100 scale
      , CULL = ifelse(
        xxxx_prop_dec > 0.5
        , CULL*100
        , CULL
      )
      , CULL = dplyr::case_when(
        CULL>100 ~ 100
        , CULL<0 ~ 0
        , T ~ CULL
      )
    ) %>% 
    # drop all temp cols
    dplyr::select(-c(xxxx_not_na_zero,xxxx_has_dec,xxxx_prop_dec))
  
  cloud2trees:::check_df_cols_all_missing(df = df, col_names = "CULL", all_numeric = T)
  
  return(df)
}

### function to set STATUSCD depending on what's in the data
cols_set_nsvb_statuscd <- function(df, default_val = 1L){
  default_val <- dplyr::coalesce(default_val, 1L)
  # STATUSCD check
  if(any(stringr::str_equal(names(df), "STATUSCD"))){
    df <- df
  }else if(any(stringr::str_equal(names(df), "statuscd"))){
    df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(STATUSCD = statuscd)
  }else if(T){ ### !!!! this just sets it to a default
    df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(STATUSCD = default_val)
  }else{
    stop(paste0(
      "the data does not contain the columns `STATUSCD` or `statuscd`"
      , "\n .... at least one of these columns must be present and have data"
    ))
  }
  
  # check valid values
  if(any( dplyr::coalesce(df$STATUSCD,0)%%1 != 0 )){stop("STATUSCD must be integer without decimal values")}
  if(!all( df$STATUSCD %in% c(1,2,3,NA) )){stop("STATUSCD must be integer value of 1, 2, or 3")}
  
  # do it as int
  df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(STATUSCD = dplyr::coalesce(as.integer(STATUSCD), default_val))
  
  cloud2trees:::check_df_cols_all_missing(df = df, col_names = "STATUSCD", all_numeric = T)
  
  return(df)
}

trees_nsvb_volume_sound <- function(
  tree_list
  , default_cull = 0
  , default_statuscd = 1L
  , drop_irrelevant = F
  ### trees_nsvb_volume_gross() inherits
  , default_stdorgcd = NA
) {
  # did this already go through trees_nsvb_volume_gross() ???
  if(
    !all(
      get_col_names_trees_nsvb_volume_gross()
      %in%
      names(tree_list)
    )
  ){
    # try to go through trees_nsvb_volume_gross() then
    message("NSVB volume columns not found...attempting to estimate with trees_nsvb_volume_gross()")
    tree_list <- trees_nsvb_volume_gross(tree_list = tree_list, default_stdorgcd = default_stdorgcd)
  }
  
  # save name for later
  orig_names_temp <- names(tree_list)

  # check data
  tree_list <- tree_list %>% 
    cols_set_nsvb_cull(default_val = default_cull) %>% 
    cols_set_nsvb_statuscd(default_val = default_statuscd) %>% 
    cols_set_nsvb_height()
  
  if(
    !all(
      c("HT", "ACTUALHT", "STATUSCD", "CULL",get_col_names_trees_nsvb_volume_gross()) %in% 
      names(tree_list)
    )
  ){
    stop("missing NSVB calculation columns in `tree_list`")
  }
  # we need a clean data set that doesn't include any variables named in any of the data used by the nsvb.Rmd data sets or functions
  # we'll start with the absolute minimum data, go through the nsvb process, drop any cols in our original data created in the process
  # then join on the new data
  # add a join id for use in combining in case any nsvb process drops rows
  tree_list <- tree_list %>% 
    dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(xxx_join_id = dplyr::row_number())
  
  tree_list_w_nsvb <- 
    tree_list %>%
    sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(
      c("xxx_join_id", "HT", "ACTUALHT", "STATUSCD", "CULL")
      , get_col_names_trees_nsvb_volume_gross()
    )))
  # save the names so we know what was added
  hey_names_temp <- names(tree_list_w_nsvb)
  
  ######################################################################################################
  # this method is defined in nsvb.Rmd
  # from https://github.com/mbrussell/NSVB
  # copied with slight adjustments
  ######################################################################################################
  tree_list_w_nsvb <- 
    tree_list_w_nsvb %>% 
    dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
    # More tree-level calcs here
    dplyr::mutate(
      V_top_bk_Sound = 0
      
      # broken tops
      
      , V_mer_ib_Sound = ((R_m_2 * V_tot_ib_Gross) - (R_1 * V_tot_ib_Gross)) * 
        (1 - CULL/100)
      , V_mer_ib_Sound2 = ((R_m_2 * V_tot_ib_Gross) - (R_1 * V_tot_ib_Gross)) * 
        (1 - 0/100)
      , V_mer_bk_Sound = ((R_m_2 * V_tot_bk_Gross) - (R_1 * V_tot_bk_Gross))
      , V_mer_ob_Sound = V_mer_ib_Sound + V_mer_bk_Sound
      , V_mer_ob_Sound2 = V_mer_ib_Sound2 + V_mer_bk_Sound
      , V_stump_ib_Sound = V_stump_ib_Gross * (1 - CULL/100)
      , V_stump_ob_Sound = V_stump_ib_Sound + V_stump_bk_Gross
      
      # Live trees
      , V_tot_ib_Sound = ifelse(
        STATUSCD == 1
        , V_tot_ib_Gross * (1 - CULL/100)
        , V_mer_ib_Sound + V_stump_ib_Sound
      )
      , V_mer_ib_Sound2 = ((R_m_2 * V_tot_ib_Gross) - (R_1 * V_tot_ib_Gross)) * 
        (1 - 0/100)
      , V_stump_ib_Sound2 = V_stump_ib_Gross * (1 - 0/100)
      , V_stump_ob_Sound2 = V_stump_ib_Sound2 + V_stump_bk_Gross
      , V_tot_ib_Sound2 = V_mer_ib_Sound2 + V_stump_ib_Sound2
      , V_tot_bk_Sound =  V_tot_bk_Gross
      , V_tot_ob_Sound = V_tot_ib_Sound + V_tot_bk_Sound
      , V_tot_bk_Sound2 =  V_tot_ob_Sound - V_tot_ib_Sound2
      , V_tot_ob_Sound2 = V_mer_ob_Sound2 + V_stump_ob_Sound2
      
      
      
      , V_tot_ob_Sound = ifelse(
        ACTUALHT == HT
        , V_tot_ib_Sound + V_tot_bk_Sound
        , V_mer_ob_Sound + V_stump_ob_Sound
      )
      , V_tot_bk_Sound = ifelse(
        ACTUALHT == HT
        , V_tot_bk_Gross
        , V_tot_ob_Sound - V_tot_ib_Sound
      )
      
      # Snags
      , V_top_ob_Sound = V_tot_ob_Sound - V_mer_ob_Sound - V_stump_ob_Sound
      , V_top_ib_Sound = V_tot_ib_Sound - V_mer_ib_Sound - V_stump_ib_Sound
      , V_top_bk = V_top_ob_Sound - V_top_ib_Sound
      
      # Missing
      , V_miss_ob_Gross = ifelse(
        V_tot_ob_Gross * (1 - R_m_2) >= 0
        , V_tot_ob_Gross * (1 - R_m_2)
        , V_tot_ob_Gross * (1 - 0)
      )
      , V_miss_ib_Gross = V_tot_ib_Gross * (1 - R_m_2)
      , V_miss_ib_Gross2 = ifelse(is.na(V_miss_ib_Gross), 0, V_miss_ib_Gross)
      , V_miss_bk_Gross = V_miss_ob_Gross - V_miss_ib_Gross2
      , V_top_ib_Sound2 = (V_tot_ib_Gross - V_mer_ib_Gross - V_stump_ib_Gross - V_miss_ib_Gross2) *
        (1-CULL/100)
      , V_top_ob_Sound2 = V_top_ib_Sound2 + V_tot_bk_Gross * 
        (1 - R_m) - V_miss_bk_Gross
      , V_top_bk_Sound2 = V_top_ob_Sound2 - V_top_ib_Sound2
      
      , V_mer_ib_Sound3 = V_mer_ib_Gross * (1 - CULL/100)
      , V_stump_ib_Sound3 = V_stump_ib_Gross * (1 - CULL/100)
      , V_tot_ib_Sound3 = (V_mer_ib_Sound3 + V_stump_ib_Sound3 + V_top_ib_Sound2)
      , V_tot_ob_Sound2 = (V_tot_ib_Sound3 + V_tot_bk_Gross - V_miss_bk_Gross)
      , V_tot_bk_Sound2 = (V_tot_ob_Sound2 - V_tot_ib_Sound3)
    )

  ######################################################################################################
  # add nsvb volume to original data
  ######################################################################################################
  new_names_temp <- base::setdiff(names(tree_list_w_nsvb),hey_names_temp)
  
  # some of these calculations resulted in negative volume values...impossible????
  # not sure if this messes up biomasss....
  ### !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! GW add ###
  tree_list_w_nsvb <- 
    tree_list_w_nsvb %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(
        .cols = dplyr::all_of(new_names_temp)
        , .fns = ~pmax(.x,0)
      ))
  ### !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! GW add end ###
  
  tree_list <-
    tree_list %>% 
    # get rid of columns we'll create
    dplyr::select( -dplyr::any_of(c(
      "hey_xxxxxxxxxx"
      , new_names_temp
    ))) %>% 
    # add nsvb data
    dplyr::left_join(
      tree_list_w_nsvb %>% dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(
        "xxx_join_id"
        , new_names_temp
      )))
      , by = "xxx_join_id"
      , relationship = "one-to-one"
    ) %>% 
    # clean up cols we may have created
    dplyr::select(-xxx_join_id) %>% 
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(
      base::setdiff(orig_names_temp,new_names_temp)
      , new_names_temp
    )))

  if(dplyr::coalesce(drop_irrelevant[1],F)){
    tree_list <- tree_list %>% 
      # get rid of irrelevant columns created for biomass
      dplyr::select( -dplyr::any_of(c(
        "hey_xxxxxxxxxx"
        , get_col_names_trees_nsvb_volume_sound_irrelevant()
      )))
  }
    
  return(tree_list)
}

# and a function that returns all of the variable names created in the trees_nsvb_volume_sound() function
get_col_names_trees_nsvb_volume_sound <- function() {
  c(
    "V_top_bk_Sound","V_mer_ib_Sound","V_mer_ib_Sound2","V_mer_bk_Sound","V_mer_ob_Sound"
    ,"V_mer_ob_Sound2","V_stump_ib_Sound","V_stump_ob_Sound","V_tot_ib_Sound","V_stump_ib_Sound2"
    ,"V_stump_ob_Sound2","V_tot_ib_Sound2","V_tot_bk_Sound","V_tot_ob_Sound","V_tot_bk_Sound2"
    ,"V_tot_ob_Sound2","V_top_ob_Sound","V_top_ib_Sound","V_top_bk","V_miss_ob_Gross","V_miss_ib_Gross"
    ,"V_miss_ib_Gross2","V_miss_bk_Gross","V_top_ib_Sound2","V_top_ob_Sound2","V_top_bk_Sound2"
    ,"V_mer_ib_Sound3","V_stump_ib_Sound3","V_tot_ib_Sound3"
  )
}
# and a function that returns all of the TEMP variable names created in the trees_nsvb_volume_sound() function
# THESE ARE COLUMNS THAT ARE USED IN BIOMASS CALCULATIONS BUT ARE IRRELEVANT IF THE USER ISN'T INTERESTED IN BIOMASS
get_col_names_trees_nsvb_volume_sound_irrelevant <- function() {
  c(
    "V_mer_ib_Sound2","V_mer_ob_Sound2","V_stump_ib_Sound2"
    ,"V_stump_ob_Sound2","V_tot_ib_Sound2","V_tot_bk_Sound2"
    ,"V_tot_ob_Sound2","V_miss_ib_Gross2","V_top_ib_Sound2"
    ,"V_top_ob_Sound2","V_top_bk_Sound2"
    ,"V_mer_ib_Sound3","V_stump_ib_Sound3","V_tot_ib_Sound3"
  )
}
```

let's take that `trees_nsvb_volume_sound()` function which relies on data loaded via `nsvb.Rmd` (which we can put in a package’s internal data in `R/sysdata.rda` with `usethis::use_data(..., internal = T)`) to take our own, custom tree list and automatically apply the gross volume calculations

note, that some of the reference data does not have tree height measurement information, so we will not be able to calculate volume for these trees since the NSVB equations rely on tree height

```{r, results=F, message=F}
# do it
ref_trees_list <- ref_trees_list %>% 
  purrr::map(function(df){
    safe_trees_nsvb_volume_sound <- purrr::safely(trees_nsvb_volume_sound)
    ans <- safe_trees_nsvb_volume_sound(df)
    if(is.null(ans$error)){
      return(ans$result)
    }else{
      return(df)
    }
  })
pred_trees_list <- pred_trees_list %>% 
  purrr::map(function(df){
    safe_trees_nsvb_volume_sound <- purrr::safely(trees_nsvb_volume_sound)
    ans <- safe_trees_nsvb_volume_sound(df)
    if(is.null(ans$error)){
      return(ans$result)
    }else{
      return(df)
    }
  })
```

let's plot the relationship between tree height and NSVB-estimated sound cubic-foot total-stem wood volume, inside bark (`V_tot_ib_Sound`) for a single site using the predicted data (because with the predicted data we'll always have DBH and height, while some reference data is missing height)

since the "sound" volume estimates are adjusted based on the `CULL` and `STATUSCD` values for each tree and we don't have this information for the predicted trees, we'll fake some dead trees in the predicted data by randomly setting ~95% trees as live (`STATUSCD = 1`) and the rest as dead (`STATUSCD = 2`) and we'll randomly set `cull` to a value above 0 for 7% of trees

## NSVB Biomass Values

let's try to figure out what we need to work with our own tree data

to get the primary **Biomass** weight (in pounds) metrics of:

| Westfall abbr      | FIADB abbr | Definition      | Units |
| ----------- | ----------- | ----------- | ----------- |
| $AGB_{Predicted}$ |	DRYBIO_AG |		Aboveground dry biomass of wood and bark      | pounds       |
| $Wood_{Harmonized}$ |	DRYBIO_STEM |		Dry biomass of wood in the total stem      | pounds      |
| $Bark_{Harmonized}$ |	DRYBIO_STEM_BARK |		Dry biomass of bark in the total stem | pounds      |
| $Branch_{Harmonized}$ |	DRYBIO_BRANCH |		Dry biomass of branches | pounds      |
| $Wfoliage$ |	DRYBIO_FOLIAGE |		Dry biomass of foliage| pounds      |
| $Wstump_{ib}$ |	DRYBIO_STUMP |		Dry biomass of wood in the stump | pounds      |
| $Wstump_{bk}$ |	DRYBIO_STUMP_BARK |		Dry biomass of bark in the stump| pounds      |
| $Wmer_{ob}$ |	DRYBIO_BOLE |		Dry biomass of wood in the merchantable bole | pounds      |
| $Wmer_{bk}$ |	DRYBIO_BOLE_BARK |		Dry biomass of bark in the merchantable bole | pounds      |
| $Vsaw_{ib}Gross x WDSG_adj x 62.4$ |	DRYBIO_SAWLOG	| Dry biomass of wood in the sawlog portion of a sawtimber tree. | pounds      |
| $Vsaw_{bk}Gross x WDSG_adj x 62.4$ |	DRYBIO_SAWLOG_BARK |	Dry biomass of bark in the sawlog portion of a sawtimber tree | pounds      |
| $C$ |	CARBON_AG	 |	Aboveground carbon of wood and bark | pounds      |

Westfall et al. ([2024](https://doi.org/10.2737/WO-GTR-104)) outline modifications and reductions applied to volume (and subsequent biomass) estimates based on wood decay classification for standing dead trees and broken top trees:

>Modifications for standing dead trees to wood density and for bark and branch losses based on the observed level of decay as indicated by the FIA decay class code (DECAYCD) variable (Burrill et al. 2023) and hardwood or softwood species classification are incorporated into the NSVB framework by adopting the findings of Harmon et al. (2011) as shown in table 1. Note that these values account for differences between hardwood and softwood species, unlike the values presented in Domke et al. (2011). The values for wood density proportion for DECAYCD = 3 are also used to account for the fact that rotten wood cull still maintains a weight greater than zero even though rotten cull is entirely deducted to obtain sound cubic volume amounts. In this case, the observed cull is assumed to be entirely rotten wood, and the density of that wood is reduced accordingly. In addition, model 6 is used to implement a standardized approach to estimate volume and biomass reductions from missing stem tops. Belowground coarse root biomass is calculated using the approach described in Heath et al. (2009) but by using merchantable stem wood volume as calculated here and applying the wood density proportions from table 1 for standing dead trees. (p. 4-5)

these biomass estimates rely on the **Gross** volume predictions detailed above as well as the tree list inputs required to calculate those predictions (`HT`, `ACTUALHT`, `DIA`, `SPCD`, `DIVISION`, `STDORGCD`) and the modified **Sound** volume predictions detailed above (and the required inputs of `CULL` and `STATUSCD`)

however, they also rely on other variables with information about the tree status which include: 

* `DECAYCD` : Decay class code indicating the stage of decay in a standing dead tree. from the [FIADB user guide](https://research.fs.usda.gov/understory/forest-inventory-and-analysis-database-user-guide-nfi):
  - `1` = All limbs and branches are present; the top of the crown is still present; all bark remains; sapwood is intact, with minimal decay; heartwood is sound and hard. 
  - `2` = There are few limbs and no fine branches; the top may be broken; a variable amount of bark remains; sapwood is sloughing with advanced decay; heartwood is sound at base but beginning to decay in the outer part of the upper bole. 
  - `3` = Only limb stubs exist; the top is broken; a variable amount of bark remains; sapwood is sloughing; heartwood has advanced decay in upper bole and is beginning at the base. 
  - `4` = Few or no limb stubs remain; the top is broken; a variable amount of bark remains; sapwood is sloughing; heartwood has advanced decay at the base and is sloughing in the upper bole. 
  - `5` = No evidence of branches remains; the top is broken; <20 percent of the bark remains; sapwood is gone; heartwood is sloughing throughout.
  - `0` = Live tree (included in `nsvb.Rmd` from [https://github.com/mbrussell/NSVB](https://github.com/mbrussell/NSVB))
* `xxx` : xxxxx from FIA.

let's define a function to get these **Biomass** values

```{r}
# tree_list <- pred_trees_list[[1]]
# tree_list %>% dplyr::glimpse()

### function to set DECAYCD depending on what's in the data
cols_set_nsvb_decaycd <- function(df, default_val = 0L){
  default_val <- dplyr::coalesce(default_val, 0L)
  # DECAYCD check
  if(any(stringr::str_equal(names(df), "DECAYCD"))){
    df <- df
  }else if(any(stringr::str_equal(names(df), "decaycd"))){
    df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(DECAYCD = decaycd)
  }else if(T){ ### !!!! this just sets it to a default
    df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(DECAYCD = default_val)
  }else{
    stop(paste0(
      "the data does not contain the columns `DECAYCD` or `decaycd`"
      , "\n .... at least one of these columns must be present and have data"
    ))
  }
  
  # check valid values
  if(any( dplyr::coalesce(df$DECAYCD,0)%%1 != 0 )){stop("DECAYCD must be integer without decimal values")}
  if(!all( df$DECAYCD %in% c(1,2,3,4,5,NA) )){stop("DECAYCD must be integer value of 1-5 or NA")}
  
  # do it as int
  df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(DECAYCD = dplyr::coalesce(as.integer(DECAYCD), default_val))
  
  cloud2trees:::check_df_cols_all_missing(df = df, col_names = "DECAYCD", all_numeric = T)
  
  return(df)
}



### function to set CULL depending on what's in the data
cols_set_nsvb_cull <- function(df, default_val = 0){
  default_val <- dplyr::coalesce(as.numeric(default_val), 0)
  # CULL check
  if(any(stringr::str_equal(names(df), "CULL"))){
    df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(CULL = as.numeric(CULL))
  }else if(any(stringr::str_equal(names(df), "cull"))){
    df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(CULL = as.numeric(cull))
  }else if(T){ ### !!!! this just sets it to a default
    df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(CULL = default_val)
  }else{
    stop(paste0(
      "the data does not contain the columns `CULL`"
      , "\n .... at least one of these columns must be present and have data"
    ))
  }
  
  ## CULL should be on 0-100 scale...check and fix if a user put it in on 0-1 scale (as decimals..)
  df <- 
    df %>% 
    dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(
      xxxx_not_na_zero = !is.na(CULL) & CULL != 0 # all values defined
      , xxxx_has_dec = xxxx_not_na_zero & (CULL%%1 != 0) & (CULL<1) # defined values less than 1 that are decimals
      # prop of vals with decimals
      , xxxx_prop_dec = sum(xxxx_has_dec, na.rm = T) / sum(xxxx_not_na_zero, na.rm = T)
      , xxxx_prop_dec = dplyr::coalesce(xxxx_prop_dec,0)
      # if over half of defined values are less than one and have decimals, convert to 0-100 scale
      , CULL = ifelse(
        xxxx_prop_dec > 0.5
        , CULL*100
        , CULL
      )
      , CULL = dplyr::case_when(
        CULL>100 ~ 100
        , CULL<0 ~ 0
        , T ~ CULL
      )
    ) %>% 
    # drop all temp cols
    dplyr::select(-c(xxxx_not_na_zero,xxxx_has_dec,xxxx_prop_dec))
  
  cloud2trees:::check_df_cols_all_missing(df = df, col_names = "CULL", all_numeric = T)
  
  return(df)
}

trees_nsvb_biomass <- function(
    tree_list
    , default_decaycd = 0L
    ### trees_nsvb_volume_sound() inherits
    , default_cull = 0
    , default_statuscd = 1L
    ### trees_nsvb_volume_gross() inherits
    , default_stdorgcd = NA
    # clean up allllll irrelevant including from trees_nsvb_volume_sound() 
    , drop_irrelevant = T
  ) {
  # did this already go through trees_nsvb_volume_sound() ???
  if(
    !all(
      get_col_names_trees_nsvb_volume_sound()
      %in%
      names(tree_list)
    ) &&
    !all(
      get_col_names_trees_nsvb_volume_gross()
      %in%
      names(tree_list)
    )
  ){
    # try to go through trees_nsvb_volume_sound() then
    message("NSVB volume columns not found...attempting to estimate with trees_nsvb_volume_sound()")
    tree_list <- trees_nsvb_volume_sound(
      tree_list = tree_list
      , default_cull = default_cull
      , default_statuscd = default_statuscd
      , default_stdorgcd = default_stdorgcd
      , drop_irrelevant = F ## needed for these biomass
    )
  }
  
  # save name for later
  orig_names_temp <- names(tree_list)

  # check data
  tree_list <- tree_list %>% 
    cols_set_nsvb_dbh() %>% 
    cols_set_nsvb_height() %>% 
    cols_set_nsvb_spcd() %>% 
    cols_set_nsvb_stdorgcd(default_val = default_stdorgcd) %>% 
    cols_set_nsvb_statuscd(default_val = default_statuscd) %>% 
    cols_set_nsvb_cull() %>% 
    cols_set_nsvb_decaycd(default_val = default_decaycd)
  
  if(
    !all(
      c(
        "SPCD", "DECAYCD", "STATUSCD", "CULL"
        , "DIA", "HT"
        , "DIVISION", "STDORGCD"
        , get_col_names_trees_nsvb_volume_gross()
        , get_col_names_trees_nsvb_volume_sound()
      ) %in% 
      names(tree_list)
    )
  ){
    stop("missing NSVB calculation columns in `tree_list`")
  }
  # we need a clean data set that doesn't include any variables named in any of the data used by the nsvb.Rmd data sets or functions
  # we'll start with the absolute minimum data, go through the nsvb process, drop any cols in our original data created in the process
  # then join on the new data
  # add a join id for use in combining in case any nsvb process drops rows
  tree_list <- tree_list %>% 
    dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(xxx_join_id = dplyr::row_number())
  
  tree_list_w_nsvb <- 
    tree_list %>%
    sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(
      c(
        "xxx_join_id"
        , "SPCD", "DECAYCD", "STATUSCD", "CULL"
        , "DIA", "HT"
        , "DIVISION", "STDORGCD"
      )
      , get_col_names_trees_nsvb_volume_gross()
      , get_col_names_trees_nsvb_volume_sound()
    )))
  # save the names so we know what was added
  hey_names_temp <- names(tree_list_w_nsvb)
  
  ######################################################################################################
  # this method is defined in nsvb.Rmd
  # from https://github.com/mbrussell/NSVB
  # copied with slight adjustments
  ######################################################################################################
  tree_list_w_nsvb <- 
    tree_list_w_nsvb %>% 
    dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
    # Enter Wood density proportions and remaining bark and branch proportions 
    # for standing dead trees (Westfall et al. 2023 Table 1)
    dplyr::left_join(wdsg, by = "SPCD", relationship = "many-to-one") %>% 
    dplyr::left_join(dead, by = c("SFTWD_HRDWD", "DECAYCD"), relationship = "many-to-one") %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(
      W_tot_ib = V_tot_ib_Gross * WDSG * 62.4
      , W_tot_ib_red = ifelse(
        SPCD < 300 & STATUSCD == 1
        , (V_tot_ib_Gross - V_miss_ib_Gross2) * 
          (1 - (CULL/100) * (1 - 0.92)) * WDSG * 62.4
        , ifelse(
          SPCD >= 300 & STATUSCD == 1
          , (V_tot_ib_Gross - V_miss_ib_Gross2) * 
            (1 - (CULL/100) * (1 - 0.54)) * WDSG * 62.4
          , #SDTs
            V_tot_ib_Sound / (1 - CULL/100) * 
            WDSG * DENS_PROP * 62.4
        )
      )
    ) %>% 
    # dplyr::select(
    #   -base::setdiff(names(wdsg),c("SPCD"))
    # ) %>% 
    # dplyr::select(
    #   -base::setdiff(names(dead),c("DECAYCD"))
    # ) %>% 
    # Estimate total stem bark weight
    dplyr::left_join(spp_bark_wt_all, by = c("DIVISION", "STDORGCD", "SPCD")) %>% 
    xxxxx # add backup join
    dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(
      W_tot_bk = get_nsvb(
        MODEL = MODEL, SPCD = SPCD
        , DIA = DIA, HT = HT
        , a = a, b = b, b1 = b1, c = c
        , WDSG = NA
      )
    ) %>% 
    dplyr::select(
      -base::setdiff(names(spp_bark_wt_all),c("DIVISION", "STDORGCD", "SPCD"))
    ) %>%

  ######################################################################################################
  # add nsvb volume to original data
  ######################################################################################################
  new_names_temp <- base::setdiff(names(tree_list_w_nsvb),hey_names_temp)
  
  # some of these calculations resulted in negative volume values...impossible????
  # not sure if this messes up biomasss....
  ### !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! GW add ###
  tree_list_w_nsvb <- 
    tree_list_w_nsvb %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(
        .cols = dplyr::all_of(new_names_temp)
        , .fns = ~pmax(.x,0)
      ))
  ### !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! GW add end ###
  
  tree_list <-
    tree_list %>% 
    # get rid of columns we'll create
    dplyr::select( -dplyr::any_of(c(
      "hey_xxxxxxxxxx"
      , new_names_temp
    ))) %>% 
    # add nsvb data
    dplyr::left_join(
      tree_list_w_nsvb %>% dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(
        "xxx_join_id"
        , new_names_temp
      )))
      , by = "xxx_join_id"
      , relationship = "one-to-one"
    ) %>% 
    # clean up cols we may have created
    dplyr::select(-xxx_join_id) %>% 
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(
      base::setdiff(orig_names_temp,new_names_temp)
      , new_names_temp
    )))

  if(dplyr::coalesce(drop_irrelevant[1],F)){
    tree_list <- tree_list %>% 
      # get rid of irrelevant columns created for biomass
      dplyr::select( -dplyr::any_of(c(
        "hey_xxxxxxxxxx"
        , get_col_names_trees_nsvb_biomass_irrelevant()
      )))
  }
    
  return(tree_list)
}

# and a function that returns all of the variable names created in the trees_nsvb_biomass() function
get_col_names_trees_nsvb_biomass <- function() {
  c(
    "V_top_bk_Sound","V_mer_ib_Sound","V_mer_ib_Sound2","V_mer_bk_Sound","V_mer_ob_Sound"
    ,"V_mer_ob_Sound2","V_stump_ib_Sound","V_stump_ob_Sound","V_tot_ib_Sound","V_stump_ib_Sound2"
    ,"V_stump_ob_Sound2","V_tot_ib_Sound2","V_tot_bk_Sound","V_tot_ob_Sound","V_tot_bk_Sound2"
    ,"V_tot_ob_Sound2","V_top_ob_Sound","V_top_ib_Sound","V_top_bk","V_miss_ob_Gross","V_miss_ib_Gross"
    ,"V_miss_ib_Gross2","V_miss_bk_Gross","V_top_ib_Sound2","V_top_ob_Sound2","V_top_bk_Sound2"
    ,"V_mer_ib_Sound3","V_stump_ib_Sound3","V_tot_ib_Sound3"
  )
}
# and a function that returns all of the TEMP variable names created in the trees_nsvb_biomass() function
# THESE ARE COLUMNS THAT ARE USED IN BIOMASS CALCULATIONS BUT ARE IRRELEVANT IF THE USER ISN'T INTERESTED IN BIOMASS
get_col_names_trees_nsvb_biomass_irrelevant <- function() {
  c(
    "V_mer_ib_Sound2","V_mer_ob_Sound2","V_stump_ib_Sound2"
    ,"V_stump_ob_Sound2","V_tot_ib_Sound2","V_tot_bk_Sound2"
    ,"V_tot_ob_Sound2","V_miss_ib_Gross2","V_top_ib_Sound2"
    ,"V_top_ob_Sound2","V_top_bk_Sound2"
    ,"V_mer_ib_Sound3","V_stump_ib_Sound3","V_tot_ib_Sound3"
  )
}
```

```{r, include=F, eval=F}
tree %>% dplyr::glimpse()
# # tree %>% dplyr::glimpse()
# ## inputs
# c(
#   "EXAMPLE"
#   , "DIVISION" # If a species occurs in an ecodivision (DIVISION) not explicitly listed, the entry having no ecodivision noted is used
#   , "PROVINCE"
#   , "STDORGCD" # stand origins for planted (stand origin code (STDORGCD) = 1) and natural (STDORGCD = 0) stands
#   , "SPCD"
#   , "DIA"
#   ,  "HT"
#   , "ACTUALHT"
#   , "CR"
#   ,  "CULL"
#   , "DECAYCD"
#   , "STATUSCD"
# )
# ## desired outputs
# # V_tot_ib_Gross # Gross cubic-foot total-stem wood volume
# # V_tot_bk_Gross # Gross cubic-foot total-stem bark volume
# # V_mer_ib_Gross # Gross cubic-foot merchantable stem wood volume (inside bark)
# # V_mer_bk_Gross # Merchantable stem bark volume
# # V_saw_ib_Gross # Gross cubic-foot wood volume in the sawlog portion of a sawtimber tree
# # V_saw_bk_Gross # cubic-foot bark volume in the sawlog portion of a sawtimber tree

# tree gets this data attached
nsvb_join_cols_temp <- c("DIVISION", "STDORGCD", "SPCD")
tree %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  dplyr::select(dplyr::any_of(c(
    c("EXAMPLE", "DIVISION", "PROVINCE", "STDORGCD", "SPCD", "DIA",  "HT", "ACTUALHT", "CR",  "CULL", "DECAYCD", "STATUSCD")
  ))) %>% 
  # 1. Gross total stem wood volume, inside bark:
  dplyr::left_join(spp_vol_ib_all, by = nsvb_join_cols_temp) %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    V_tot_ib_Gross = get_nsvb(
      MODEL = MODEL
      , SPCD = SPCD
      , DIA = DIA
      , HT = HT
      , a = a, a1 = a1, b = b
      , b1 = b1, c = c, c1 = c1
      , WDSG = NA
    )
    , 
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::select(
    -base::setdiff(names(spp_vol_ib_all),nsvb_join_cols_temp) 
  ) %>% 
  # 2. Gross total stem bark volume
  dplyr::left_join(spp_vol_bark_all, by = nsvb_join_cols_temp) %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    V_tot_bk_Gross = get_nsvb(
      MODEL = MODEL
      , SPCD = SPCD
      , DIA = DIA
      , HT = HT
      , a = a, a1 = a1, b = b
      , b1 = b1, c = c, c1 = c1
      , WDSG = NA
    )
    # 3. Gross total stem outside-bark volume
    , V_tot_ob_Gross = V_tot_ib_Gross + V_tot_bk_Gross
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::select(
    -base::setdiff(names(spp_vol_bark_all),nsvb_join_cols_temp) 
  ) %>% 
  # 4. Estimate height to merchantable top diameter (4.0-inch)
  dplyr::left_join(spp_vol_ob_all, by = nsvb_join_cols_temp) %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    hm = ifelse(
      DIA >= 5 #### !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! convert cm to inches
      , get_hm(
        top_dia = 4
        , a = a, b = b, c = c
        , alpha = alpha, beta = beta
        , DIA = DIA, HT = HT
      )
      , NA
    )
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::select(
    -base::setdiff(names(spp_vol_ob_all),nsvb_join_cols_temp) 
  ) %>% 
  # 5. Estimate merchantable wood volume – volume ratios to stump & merchantable top
  dplyr::left_join(spp_vol_ratio_all, by = nsvb_join_cols_temp) %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    R_1 = get_V_ratio(h1 = 1, HT = HT, alpha = alpha, beta = beta)
    , R_m = ifelse(
      DIA >= 5  #### !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! convert cm to inches
      , get_V_ratio(
        h1 = hm, HT = HT
        , alpha = alpha, beta = beta
      )
      , NA
    )
    , R_m_2 = get_V_ratio(
      h1 = ACTUALHT, HT = HT
      , alpha = alpha, beta = beta
    )
    , V_mer_ib_Gross = (R_m * V_tot_ib_Gross ) - (R_1 * V_tot_ib_Gross)
    , V_mer_ob_Gross = (R_m * V_tot_ob_Gross ) - (R_1 * V_tot_ob_Gross)
    , V_mer_bk_Gross = V_mer_ob_Gross - V_mer_ib_Gross
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::select(
    -base::setdiff(names(spp_vol_ratio_all),nsvb_join_cols_temp) 
  ) %>% 
  # Volume in the sawlog portion of the stem
  dplyr::left_join(spp_vol_ob_all, by = nsvb_join_cols_temp) %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    hm_saw = ifelse(
      SPCD < 300 & DIA >= 9.0  #### !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! convert cm to inches
      , get_hm(
        top_dia = 7  #### !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! convert cm to inches
        , a = a, b = b, c = c
        , alpha = alpha, beta = beta
        , DIA = DIA, HT = HT
      )
      , ifelse(
        SPCD >= 300 & DIA >= 11.0  #### !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! convert cm to inches
        , get_hm(
          top_dia = 9  #### !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! convert cm to inches
          , a = a, b = b, c = c
          , alpha = alpha, beta = beta
          , DIA = DIA, HT = HT
        )
        , NA
      )
    )
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::select(
    -base::setdiff(names(spp_vol_ob_all),nsvb_join_cols_temp) 
  ) %>% 
  # Sawlog volumes ratios - stump and merchantable height
  dplyr::left_join(spp_vol_ratio_all, by = nsvb_join_cols_temp) %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    R_s = get_V_ratio(
      h1 = hm_saw
      , HT = HT
      , alpha = alpha
      , beta = beta
    )
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::select(
    -base::setdiff(names(spp_vol_ratio_all),nsvb_join_cols_temp) 
  ) %>% 
  # More tree-level calcs here
  #### GW add.... i'm going to break this into columns that require CULL and those that don't
  dplyr::mutate(
    V_saw_ib_Gross = (R_s * V_tot_ib_Gross) - (R_1 * V_tot_ib_Gross)
    , V_saw_ob_Gross = (R_s * V_tot_ob_Gross) - (R_1 * V_tot_ob_Gross)
    , V_saw_bk_Gross = V_saw_ob_Gross - V_saw_ib_Gross
    , V_stump_ob_Gross = (R_1 * V_tot_ob_Gross)
    , V_stump_ib_Gross = (R_1 * V_tot_ib_Gross)
    , V_stump_bk_Gross = V_stump_ob_Gross - V_stump_ib_Gross
    , V_top_ob_Gross = V_tot_ob_Gross - V_mer_ob_Gross - V_stump_ob_Gross
    , V_top_ib_Gross = V_tot_ib_Gross - V_mer_ib_Gross - V_stump_ib_Gross
    , V_top_bk_Gross = V_top_ob_Gross - V_top_ib_Gross
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    CULL = ifelse(is.na(CULL), 0, CULL)
    , V_top_bk_Sound = 0
    # broken tops
    , V_mer_ib_Sound = ((R_m_2 * V_tot_ib_Gross) - (R_1 * V_tot_ib_Gross)) * 
        (1 - CULL/100)
    , V_mer_ib_Sound2 = ((R_m_2 * V_tot_ib_Gross) - (R_1 * V_tot_ib_Gross)) # * (1 - 0/100)
    , V_mer_bk_Sound = ((R_m_2 * V_tot_bk_Gross) - (R_1 * V_tot_bk_Gross))
    , V_mer_ob_Sound = V_mer_ib_Sound + V_mer_bk_Sound
    , V_mer_ob_Sound2 = V_mer_ib_Sound2 + V_mer_bk_Sound
    , V_stump_ib_Sound = V_stump_ib_Gross * (1 - CULL/100)
    , V_stump_ob_Sound = V_stump_ib_Sound + V_stump_bk_Gross
  ) %>% 
  #### GW add.... i'm going to break this into columns that require STATUSCD and those that don't
  #### GW add.... i'm going to break this into columns that require ACTUALHT and those that don't
  dplyr::mutate(
    STATUSCD = dplyr::coalesce(as.numeric(STATUSCD), 1) #### GW add....
    # Live trees
    , V_tot_ib_Sound = ifelse(
      STATUSCD == 1
      , V_tot_ib_Gross * (1 - CULL/100)
      , V_mer_ib_Sound + V_stump_ib_Sound
    )
    , V_mer_ib_Sound2 = ((R_m_2 * V_tot_ib_Gross) - (R_1 * V_tot_ib_Gross)) #* (1 - 0/100)
    , V_stump_ib_Sound2 = V_stump_ib_Gross * (1 - 0/100)
    , V_stump_ob_Sound2 = V_stump_ib_Sound2 + V_stump_bk_Gross
    , V_tot_ib_Sound2 = V_mer_ib_Sound2 + V_stump_ib_Sound2
    , V_tot_bk_Sound =  V_tot_bk_Gross
    , V_tot_ob_Sound = V_tot_ib_Sound + V_tot_bk_Sound
    , V_tot_bk_Sound2 =  V_tot_ob_Sound - V_tot_ib_Sound2,
    , V_tot_ob_Sound2 = V_mer_ob_Sound2 + V_stump_ob_Sound2
    , V_tot_ob_Sound = ifelse(
      ACTUALHT == HT
      , V_tot_ib_Sound + V_tot_bk_Sound
      , V_mer_ob_Sound + V_stump_ob_Sound
    )
    , V_tot_bk_Sound = ifelse(
      ACTUALHT == HT
      , V_tot_bk_Gross
      , V_tot_ob_Sound - V_tot_ib_Sound
    )
    ,
    # Snags
    , V_top_ob_Sound = V_tot_ob_Sound - V_mer_ob_Sound - V_stump_ob_Sound
    , V_top_ib_Sound = V_tot_ib_Sound - V_mer_ib_Sound - V_stump_ib_Sound
    , V_top_bk = V_top_ob_Sound - V_top_ib_Sound
    # Missing
    , V_miss_ob_Gross = ifelse(
      V_tot_ob_Gross * (1 - R_m_2) >= 0
      , V_tot_ob_Gross * (1 - R_m_2)
      , V_tot_ob_Gross * (1 - 0)
    )
    , V_miss_ib_Gross = V_tot_ib_Gross * (1 - R_m_2)
    , V_miss_ib_Gross2 = ifelse(is.na(V_miss_ib_Gross), 0, V_miss_ib_Gross)
    , V_miss_bk_Gross = V_miss_ob_Gross - V_miss_ib_Gross2
    , V_top_ib_Sound2 = 
      (V_tot_ib_Gross - V_mer_ib_Gross - V_stump_ib_Gross - V_miss_ib_Gross2) * 
      (1-CULL/100)
    , V_top_ob_Sound2 = V_top_ib_Sound2 + V_tot_bk_Gross * (1 - R_m) - V_miss_bk_Gross
    , V_top_bk_Sound2 = V_top_ob_Sound2 - V_top_ib_Sound2
    , V_mer_ib_Sound3 = V_mer_ib_Gross * (1 - CULL/100)
    , V_stump_ib_Sound3 = V_stump_ib_Gross * (1 - CULL/100)
    , V_tot_ib_Sound3 = (V_mer_ib_Sound3 + V_stump_ib_Sound3 + V_top_ib_Sound2)
    , V_tot_ob_Sound2 = (V_tot_ib_Sound3 + V_tot_bk_Gross - V_miss_bk_Gross)
    , V_tot_bk_Sound2 = (V_tot_ob_Sound2 - V_tot_ib_Sound3)
  ) %>% 
  # Enter Wood density proportions and remaining bark and branch proportions 
  # for standing dead trees (Westfall et al. 2023 Table 1)
  #### GW add.... i'm going to break this into columns that require DECAYCD and those that don't
  dplyr::mutate(DECAYCD = ifelse(is.na(DECAYCD), 0, DECAYCD)) %>% 
  dplyr::left_join(wdsg, by = "SPCD") %>% 
  dplyr::left_join(dead, by = c("SFTWD_HRDWD", "DECAYCD")) %>% 
  dplyr::glimpse()
```
